title: Database write placed inside a Kafka transaction — an atomicity boundary Kafka cannot cover
code_snippet:
Design note from the RFC under review:

  To make the order insert and the order.created event atomic we will use
  Kafka transactions so the DB write and the outbox publish commit together:
  initTransaction / beginTransaction around both, so either both land or
  neither does.
expected_feedback: Critical: this describes something Kafka cannot do. A Kafka transaction spans Kafka partitions and consumer offset commits only — it has no visibility into a PostgreSQL row and cannot roll one back. Wrapping a db.Exec in beginTransaction/commitTransaction compiles and runs while providing none of the claimed atomicity: a failure after the DB commit and before commitTransaction leaves the row written and the event absent. Use the outbox pattern instead: business rows and the outbox row commit in ONE database transaction, then a separate relay reads unpublished rows, produces to Kafka, waits for the broker ack, and only then marks them published. Order those two relay steps that way — marking first turns a crash into permanent event loss. The outbox is at-least-once by construction (publish and mark are two commits), so consumers still need idempotency; it removes the dual-write window, not the dedup requirement.
violated_rule: Atomicity mechanism matches the boundary being crossed
checklist_anchor: **A Kafka transaction cannot include a database write.**
